finding: The published canonical answers for the APSTATS-SFRQ-* family are the rubric's own learner_facing_text, not student answers. They are written in third-person rubric voice with criterion-key prefixes -- "a1) States the median is 22 minutes." rather than "The median commute time is 22 minutes." This is live Production content that Open Hand shows students as the full-credit exemplar. It is NOT a work order C defect: C was instructed to preserve existing text verbatim and did so correctly.
evidence: Measured over 134 span-by-criterion pairs after stripping the a1)/b1) prefixes: mean word-level similarity to the criterion's own learner_facing_text is 0.405 overall, and 0.652 for the APSTATS-SFRQ family, where 28 of 56 pairs are at or above 0.85. 32 pairs are at or above 0.95, several character-identical -- e.g. APSTATS-SFRQ-013 [a], answer and criterion are both exactly "States H0: mu = 70 and Ha: mu != 70." 18 of the 34 in-scope items carry at least one such span; all 14 SFRQ items do.
recommended_action: Product Owner decision on re-authoring these 14 SFRQ canonical answers as student-voice answers. They are the same defect class work order B was explicitly warned about ("rubric restatements, not answers"), except already published rather than proposed. Until then these items should not be used as grading exemplars.

C flagged 26 items for uncovered criteria and span entanglement but raised nothing about the answers being rubric prose, even while segmenting text whose spans match their criteria near-verbatim.
evidence: open_questions.csv holds 12 uncovered-criteria rows and one judgment row (C-J01) about graph literalism. No row mentions answer voice or rubric duplication. C's SUMMARY.md likewise does not raise it.
recommended_action: No rework. Record so the next segmentation order carries an explicit check: if a span is near-identical to the criterion it earns, the source content -- not the segmentation -- is the finding.

finding: CORRECTED 2026-09-23 after Product Owner challenge. An earlier version of this finding said the spatial criteria are "structurally unearnable by text" and questioned C's scoping. That framing was wrong: hand-drawn capture exists precisely so these criteria CAN be earned, and the spatial canonical already exists in content. The real finding is that the scoring path is declared but not wired. All 24 published hand-drawn items carry evaluator_strategy='human_shadow', which resolves to routing target 'shadow_review' -- a hold that awards no points -- while production does no human grading. So today a student can capture the drawing and the attempt holds rather than scores.
evidence: Verified read-only in Production: capture infrastructure is live (app.capture_pairing_tokens 3 rows, app.capture_pairing_events 5 rows, learner-uploads bucket). The spatial canonical exists on every one of the 24 items as prompt_json.expected_graph_spec (24/24). rubric_type='spatial' on 23 of 24. Routing confirmed in code: supabase/functions/_shared/grading-router.ts maps rubric_type 'spatial' and strategy 'human_shadow' to target 'shadow_review'; supabase/functions/evaluate-attempt/index.ts line 1482 comments that the item is "held for human/shadow review until the declared verifier is wired in" and awards no points.
recommended_action: Product Owner call on sequencing Engine 4's verifier, not a C defect and not a content defect. C marked the text-side criteria uncovered correctly -- the drawing covers them, not the prose. Track as the blocker it is: the content and the capture are ready; the spatial verifier is the missing piece.

evidence: Production read-only: 19 of 20 ap-statistics hand-drawn items have rubric_type='spatial', 1 null; all 4 biology ones have it. The router (grading-router.ts) reads rubric_type first and falls back to prompt_json evaluator_strategy, which this item does carry.
recommended_action: Fold into work order I.2, which already scopes rubric_type coverage. No rework of C.

finding: expected_graph_spec may be too thin to verify every spatial criterion it has to serve. GRAPH-005's spec is {x_axis: 'hours studied', y_axis: 'test score', representation: 'scatterplot with trend line'} -- enough to check AXIS_LABELS, but it does not carry the nine ordered pairs that criterion POINTS_PLOTTED ("Plots all nine ordered pairs at recoverable locations") requires a verifier to check against.
evidence: Compared each item's expected_graph_spec against its own stored spatial criterion keys. The data points appear in stimulus_table rather than in the spec, so a verifier would have to join the two.
recommended_action: Before Engine 4's verifier is built, audit all 24 expected_graph_spec values against the spatial criteria they must support, and decide whether the spec should carry the expected data or reference stimulus_table. Cheaper to settle now than after the verifier is written.

finding: 38 of 108 covered criteria (35%) have no span of their own, so striking one removes text earning another. Mean over-strike is 0.35. This is materially better than work order B's 81% and 0.82, and here the entanglement is inherent to published prose C is forbidden to rewrite rather than a segmentation choice.
evidence: 21 of 105 spans (20%) carry more than one criterion key. C flagged every affected item -- 14 items carry an explicit "span(s) credit multiple criteria" flag naming the count.
recommended_action: No action against C. Fold into the same Open Hand strike-behaviour decision as B-QA-001; unlike B, this one cannot be fixed by re-cutting spans without re-authoring the published answers.
